You live in the UK.
You are asking about Child Benefit for 1 child:
  - Alex is 16 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 16 and in approved education
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to understand your situation. 

**Do you have a child or children you're claiming for?** If yes, could you tell me:
- Their name(s)
- Their age(s)

This will help me determine which eligibility path applies to your situation. Children under 16 generally qualify automatically (with some conditions), while those aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes! I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 16 years old and lives with me at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex who is 16 years old and lives with you.

Since Alex is 16, he falls into the 16-19 age category. For children in this age group, eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training, or if they've recently left and are within an extension period.

Let me ask you: **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

This includes:
- Full-time non-advanced education (like A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQ Level 3 or below)
- Approved training programs (like traineeships or certain vocational courses)

The education/training must be for more than 12 hours per week on average (excluding breaks).

Or, if he's recently left education/training, has it been less than 20 weeks since he left?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is in approved education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Alex is studying for his A-levels at sixth form college, which is approved full-time non-advanced education. This means he can still qualify as a child for Child Benefit purposes.

Let me move forward with the assessment based on this information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! A-levels at sixth form college are approved non-advanced education. Now I need to check a few more things:

**Is Alex working at all?** Specifically, I need to know if he's working 24 hours or more per week on average while studying. 

Part-time work under 24 hours per week is fine and won't affect eligibility, but full-time work (24+ hours) would make him ineligible.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's focused on his studies right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Since Alex is in approved education (A-levels) and not working full-time, let me continue through the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now, **is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right?** 

Specifically, benefits like:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Income Support
- Tax credits

If Alex is claiming any of these benefits in his own name (not as part of your household claim), this would affect eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a student living at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now, **is Alex doing an apprenticeship?** Or is he just doing regular A-levels at sixth form?

I need to check this because most apprenticeships would disqualify him from Child Benefit (except for Foundation Apprenticeships in Wales, which are still approved).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not doing an apprenticeship. He's just doing regular A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is doing regular A-levels, so that's fine. Now let me move on to questions about you as the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. **Do you normally live in the UK?** 

This is the most straightforward way to meet the residency requirement. If you're normally resident in the UK, you'll meet this requirement. 

There are also other ways to qualify (like having settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or being a Crown servant abroad), but most people qualify simply by normally living in the UK.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You're normally resident in the UK (in Manchester), so you meet the residency requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Now, you mentioned that Alex lives with you at home. This means you meet the "responsibility for the child" requirement, as you're living with him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** 

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation. You mentioned he lives with you at home in Manchester. 

**Is Alex currently:**
- In hospital (as an inpatient)?
- In local authority care?
- Being fostered?
- Or living normally at home with you?

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like he's living normally at home with you, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's living normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, not in care, and not fostered.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! One final question: **Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

Since Alex lives at home with you and is just a regular student, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm this to complete the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. He just lives at home with me and I support him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me complete the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Result: ELIGIBLE**

You meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements for your son Alex. Here's why:

✅ **Alex qualifies as a child** - He's 16 and studying A-levels (approved non-advanced education)  
✅ **Not working full-time** - He's focused on his studies  
✅ **Not receiving benefits** - He doesn't claim benefits in his own right  
✅ **Not in an apprenticeship** - He's doing regular A-levels  
✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You normally live in the UK (Manchester)  
✅ **You're responsible for him** - He lives with you at home  
✅ **No other claimant** - Nobody else is claiming for Alex  
✅ **Council not paying** - The local council isn't contributing to his care

---

## Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge**: If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay a tax charge. Between £60,000-£80,000, the charge gradually increases until it equals the benefit amount.
5. **Payments**: Child Benefit is typically paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

You can apply here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
